oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Sistema de indicadores de qualidade ambiental urbana e bem-estar para o município de Bombinhas (Santa Catarina): uma aplicação dos Objetivos do Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ODS)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The municipality of Bombinhas has an economy based on sun and sea tourism, which has boosted urban development, especially through the civil construction sector, leading to changes in environmental quality and the well-being of the resident population. This research proposes a system of Urban Environmental Quality and Well-Being Indicators for the municipality of Bombinhas (Santa Catarina), based on the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The methodology was developed in four stages: I- Systematic data collection from Bombinhas/SC; II- Adaptation of national indicators to the local scale; III- Validation and definition of the Indicator System with local stakeholders; IV- Validation of the Indicator System for Bombinhas/SC. A total of 134 indicators were defined based on data adapted to the local reality, from which 49 indicators were selected by local actors to compose the system. The results indicate that, despite tourism being the main socioeconomic dynamic, its intensity generates demand peaks that directly affect urban services such as transport, sanitation, water supply, and health, negatively impacting quality of life. The study demonstrates that, to address the challenges of urban growth, it is essential to integrate the indicators into the formulation of public policies that promote efficient resource management, the expansion of basic infrastructure, and urban resilience. The evaluated indicators highlight that the biggest challenges are related to a new way of evaluating urban development through safer and more sustainable actions, as various local administrations have left a high risk to the fair social, economic, and environmental development of the municipality.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La diversité des pédagogies alternatives en francophonie : une tentative de définition intégrative
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines alternative pedagogies in the early 21st-century French-speaking educational context, drawing on academic work that questions the practices identified in the current of “alternative” or “different” pedagogies. Our analysis highlights several constitutive and interdependent dimensions of these pedagogies: socio-political anchors, the student-centered approach, the diversity of teaching-learning practices, as well as the evolution and hybridization of pedagogical practices. On this basis, the article proposes an integrative definition that highlights the complexity and heterogeneity of alternative pedagogies, while highlighting the common dimensions that connect them. It offers a flexible analytical framework capable of considering the diversity of these pedagogies, including cases at the border between alternative and traditional pedagogy. This approach helps to clarify debates on the practices and conceptions of alternative pedagogies, while providing a useful working definition for their study.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Pierre Bourdieu et Albert Bandura, système scolaire, domination et émancipation du sujet
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The aim of the French republican schools is to train autonomous citizens by guaranteeing everyone equal access to knowledge. Yet the persistent gaps in success between pupils from different social backgrounds call into question the real scope of this principle of equality. Based on these issues, the sociologist Pierre Bourdieu and the psychologist Albert Bandura propose two divergent readings of the relationship between individuals and educational structures. The first, rooted in a sociology of reproduction, highlights the mechanisms of symbolic domination and the unconscious internalisation of habitus that limit the room for manoeuvre of social agents within the school system. The second, on the other hand, places the emphasis on the capacity for self-regulation, vicarious learning and individual agentivity, through which individuals can actively influence their environment. This theoretical confrontation makes it possible to rethink the conditions of emancipation in the field of education: is the subject solely shaped by social structures (Bourdieusian approach), or does he or she have an effective capacity to influence them (Bandurian approach)? Analysis of the notions of transmission, normative internalisation and situated action highlights the tensions between social determinism and the autonomy of the learner. It is in the way in which each pupil perceives, appropriates or deflects school rules — depending on whether they submit to them or develop strategies of resilience — that the possibility of acting in and on an education system that is a source of inequality is at stake.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines conspiracy beliefs in education using a mixed-methods design that combines international comparisons, verbal evocations, and interviews. The quantitative survey includes 1,118 preservice teachers in England, Greece, and France. Results show higher levels in Greece, intermediate levels in England, and lower levels in France, alongside stronger perceived rationality in France. Part 2 focuses on French participants and examines social representations of the “conspiracist student” through a free-evocation task. Correspondence analysis reveals two major axes (critical rationality vs disqualification/ignorance and institutional trust vs suspicion/manipulation). Part 3 draws on 19 interviews with in-service teachers in France. Teachers report infrequent yet destabilizing episodes, distrust toward institutions, and tensions with the classroom framework. They mobilize media and information literacy practices but note constraints related to time, training, and legitimacy. We discuss implications for initial and continuing teacher education to prevent the spread of conspiracy beliefs in schools.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Comment des enseignants du secondaire au Québec prennent-ils en considération les problématiques socioscientifiques et gèrent-ils les visions du monde dans les cours de sciences ?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Science education cannot continue to be largely dominated by the transmission of consensual and standardized knowledge, while science as it is done is crossed by disagreements and controversies and when conveys important social issues that mobilize plural understandings, explanations and solutions within the scientific community and in society. In addition, science offers a worldview, based on rationality and analysis of facts, which is not always compatible with other worldviews that learners may adhere to, such as religious views. In connection with this issue, we conducted interviews with secondary school science teachers to understand how 1) they take into consideration socio-scientific issues in their teaching and 2) they manage the contestation of scientific subjects or content by students who adhere to non-scientific worldviews. The results show, on the one hand, that teachers integrate certain environmental issues into their teaching, while allowing students to open up to certain aspects of argumentation. They also show that certain science contents are contested in the classroom, particularly human biology content related to sexuality as well as evolution and the origin and history of the Earth and the universe. Based on these results, the article also proposes avenues aimed at equipping teachers to face the challenges encountered in these contexts.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Co-teaching aligns with the international movement toward inclusive educational practices. This article presents an exploratory survey in a French school district on co-teaching approaches declared by general primary education teachers (n= 144) and special education teachers (n= 37) from specialized support networks for students with learning difficulties (RASED). It also explores the reasons behind their choice of specific approaches. Data were collected through a self-administered questionnaire. Closed-ended questions underwent statistical analysis, while open-ended responses were subject to thematic analysis. Results indicate that all co-teaching approaches described in the literature are reported as used, with variations in frequency depending on whether respondents are general or special education teachers. Participants attribute their choices to challenges related to the implementation of co-teaching, instructional practices and knowledge structuring, and the overall pedagogical organization of schools.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Conceptions du droit, des libertés et de la citoyenneté chez de jeunes cégépiens lors de la pandémie de COVID 19
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines CEGEP (college) students’ conceptions of law—particularly rights and freedoms—and of citizenship in Quebec during the COVID-19 pandemic. It analyzes, on the one hand, the norms and limits they deemed acceptable or unacceptable in the pandemic context, and, on the other, their understandings of civic duties as well as their perceptions of authoritative versus less credible discourses. Drawing on a legal consciousness approach (Legal Consciousness Studies), the article traces how everyday situations during the pandemic were interpreted through the lens of law (and rights and freedoms) and citizenship, and how students’ conceptions of law and justice translated into different stances (compliance, negotiation, contestation). Building on the typologies developed by Patricia Ewick and Susan Silbey (1998) and Joel Westheimer and Joseph Kahne (2004), the analysis provides a portrait of young people’s subjective relationship to law, justice, and citizenship, illustrating how they interpreted and rendered law meaningful in their daily lives during the pandemic.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Critères de démarcation de la science et sensibilisation des jeunes aux théories du complot et à la désinformation : pistes de réflexion
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: With a view to raising young people's awareness of various forms of misinformation, it is important to be able to define, albeit in a partial, provisional and critical manner, criteria for demarcating science. The aim of the first part of this article is therefore to list, in the form of a summary note, various possible criteria for demarcating science. The second part aims to examine the relevance of these criteria when it comes, more specifically, to differentiating between scientific discourse and disinformation discourse (fake news and conspiracy theory). To this end, a case study is proposed to put these criteria to the test in relation to a concrete example of conspiracy theory. Finally, the third part addresses the didactic aspects and examines, for illustrative purposes, in the case of French-speaking Belgium, the extent to which these criteria are or are not considered in the curricula for teaching science or philosophy and citizenship.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The emergence of conspiracy thinking in public debates, which shifted from the margins to the mainstream over the course of the Covid-19 pandemic, has profoundly disrupted contemporary societies, including the educational sphere. The primary objective of the study presented in this article is to examine Quebec students’ perceptions of traditional institutions—most notably the school system—and, more specifically, their understandings of conspiracy theories. This qualitative research, conducted by Stéphanie Tremblay and her colleagues (2021-2023), was carried out in three pre-university institutions (cégeps) located in the suburban area of Montreal (Quebec) through semi-structured interviews with 44 students. Thematic analysis revealed, among other findings, the significant role of emotional and relational dimensions in shaping students’ relationships with institutions and knowledge, as well as the centrality of a desire for agency among youth. The discussion then addresses the practical implications of these findings within educational contexts, particularly in light of the new Citizenship and Quebec Culture (CCQ) program introduced in 2024 in Quebec’s primary and secondary schools.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Des élèves qui parlent au nom de l’École contre l’École. Analyse d’un conflit de régime de vérités autour des politiques publiques LGBTIQ en Suisse romande
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article analyzes a controversy sparked by a blog created by students at a high school in Vaud in 2023: “Swiss Conservative Action Group” (GACS). In it, the students denounce public policies to combat discrimination against LGBTIQ students in their school as propaganda. Based on a discourse analysis, the article demonstrates how these students mobilize the school values of neutrality, freedom of expression, and critical thinking to challenge, from within, the institutional missions enshrined in school frameworks and missions (LEO, PER, RGy). By combining the concept of “regimes of truths” and the logics of justification, the article highlights how the GACS redefines these values according to its own axiological visions by mobilizing discursive registers and rhetorical strategies that are naturalistic, victimizing, conspiratorial, or based on moral panic. Finally, analysis of the GACS's arguments shows that the disagreement is less about the definition of freedom of expression or neutrality as such than about the legitimacy of schools to promote fundamental rights.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Édito - Quand les repères se brouillent : l’École ultramoderne à l’épreuve des conflits de vérités
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This special issue situates the contemporary rise of “conflicts of truths” within a broader context marked by declining trust in democratic institutions, the pluralization of sources of legitimacy, and the growing competition between expert and lay knowledge. Using conspiracy theories as an analytical lens, it shows how these narratives reveal deeper tensions among science, religion, politics, and education, particularly in a context of ultramodernity. The COVID-19 pandemic has intensified these dynamics by exposing science “in the making” and by multiplying controversies surrounding risk, rights, public health, and authority. The issue proposes to conceptualize these tensions through the notion of “regimes of truths,” understood as historically situated forms of power/knowledge that may intersect, hybridize, or come into conflict in contemporary societies. In this context, the school emerges as a central site where these epistemic and axiological reconfigurations unfold, as it is tasked with transmitting knowledge, fostering citizenship, and accommodating diverse worldviews. The special issue aims to bring into dialogue three often compartmentalized fields of research: socioscientific controversies, the relationship between scientific knowledge and religious beliefs, and critical or postmodern approaches to truth. Drawing on contributions from diverse national and disciplinary contexts, it examines how students and teachers perceive these tensions, while also proposing pedagogical and didactic approaches to addressing them in educational settings.

Burn all the records of the realm. My mouth shall be the Parliament of England,” or “our forefathers had no other books but the score and the tally.” Analysing Cade’s language, which is imbued with biblical quotations and legal traditions, and by examining the multiple manifestations of the materiality of written culture within the play, this study seeks to understand the enigmatic, paradoxical and unstable portrayal the play offers of the rebellion led by Jack Cade and the Kentish artisans in 1450. The playwright or playwrights (Shakespeare and Marlowe ? Peele ? Greene ?) have interwoven lexicons, brought eras into collision, and attributed to a framed and insignificant character the very words of egalitarian revolts. It is these ambiguities and contradictions that explain the critical disagreements regarding the meaning of these scenes, as well as their diverse and contradictory theatrical stagings.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: From 1701 until the French Revolution, any work published through legal channels was required to be reviewed by a royal censor. This review was explicitly indicated by the presence of an “approval” in the paratext. This text, combining set formulas with a space for free expression, became an easy target for parody. Throughout the century, some authors inserted fake approvals in the margins of their works, mimicking official certificates while subverting them. These forged endorsements provide valuable insight into how censorship was perceived and received by writers and readers alike, through their layout choices, use of humour, and the invention of fictitious censors.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: “In my wood to dwell”: Margaret Cavendish’s Ecocritical Thinking and her Uses of Allegory in Poetry
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Margaret Cavendish is now routinely enrolled as an early example of an eco-conscious author, and studied through the perspective lens of ecocritical approaches, but the risk of anachronism is strong. Her ecocriticism needs to be reassessed in light of her philosophical conception of nature. This article aims at contextualising her professed concern for the natural world in relation to the literary tradition of prosopopeias of trees, seventeenth-century politics and her philosophical conception of nature, looking in particular at one of her 1653 dialogues, a long poem of 164 lines in rhymed pentameters entitled “A Dialogue between an Oak and a Man Cutting Him Down”. This poem, which includes the tree’s plea to the feller not to be hacked, has comfortably been read in recent critical studies in an ecocritical perspective. Yet the convention of the tree prosopopeia, which goes back to the Bible and Ovid, had already been used by Drayton, among others, in his popular Poly-Olbion (1619). Placing Cavendish’s approach within this tradition allows us to better understand the articulation between her genuine concern for the natural world, political allegory and her natural philosophy. Focusing on Cavendish’s complex allegorical technique in the poem, this article studies her discursive uses of the oak as a multifaceted emblem, which requires hermeneutic agility on the part of the readers – and proves once more, if need be, that her poetry is more sophisticated than was once thought.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article focuses on a late, unfinished and unpublished treatise by Jeremy Bentham entitled “Auto-Icon; or, Farther Uses of the Dead to the Living”, in which the tree of knowledge, the tree of law (arbor jurisdictionis) and the genealogical tree are interwoven. The Auto-Icons – or effigies – of philosophers and legal theorists were to be brought in conversation, comparing their positions on topics such as learning, law and legacies. On epistemological matters, Bentham sought to correct the failings of earlier models of tree diagrams, but remained convinced that the tree was the best model to offer an overview of the structure of arts and sciences. The tree proved as much a resource as a challenge, raising questions about its composition, orientation, ornamentation, as well as the desirable number of subdivisions. Answering such questions led Bentham to position himself in a genealogy of philosophers. But the tree is also very much present in the discussion of the “commemorational” uses to which Auto-Icons could be put, not least because woods and trees played a key role in the construction of the Common Law tradition as an unbroken patrilinear genealogy. Through the use of irony and satire, Bentham seems to mock both the pretensions of the nobility and, in a reflective gesture, his own bid for posthumous fame. With its excesses and oddities, “Auto-Icon” reminds readers that the tree is not a “natural” metaphor and that its various uses have a history, which needs to be traced so as to contextualize the ideology such uses convey.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Trees in William Cowper’s Poetry
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article tackles how William Cowper (1731-1800) uses trees in The Task (1783-1784), “The Poplar Field” (1783-1784?), and “Yardley Oak,” an unfinished poem from 1791, as figures of the expressive and the emblematical. The British poet has recourse to a set of artistic traits, borrowing from pictorial, architectural and musical techniques to make trees a fulcrum of his landscape descriptions. The interplay of colours, as well as light and shade, are two of the techniques he uses to capture variations in tones and shapes, while expressing his admiration for the beauty of trees. Yet that does not prevent him from lamenting the transformation of the landscape he dearly loves as a result of human intervention – the felling of poplars being the most obvious example –, in addition to the growing distance between trees and people, who no longer take advantage of the shade the former give. Besides, trees exemplify Cowper’s reflection about what time and human life stand for, giving him the opportunity to steer his poems in a meditative direction: the oak and poplar, to which he devoted specific texts, reflect the poet’s condition, and are furthermore a mirror of human frailty and mortality, as reflected in his analogy between the human body and a tree’s branches and trunk, which both grow before declining.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La critique de l’ethnocentrisme dans les Nouveaux Mémoires sur l’état présent de la Chine de Louis Le Comte (1696)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Back in France, Jesuit missionary Louis Le Comte published his Nouveaux Mémoires sur l’état présent de la Chine in 1696. His admiring remarks on the religion of the ancient Chinese caused such a scandal that the Sorbonne censored the work in 1700. In the Nouveaux Mémoires, Le Comte undertakes a critique of ethnocentrism, initially directed at the collective “vanity” of the Chinese, then subtly turned against France itself. In his view, both China and France display flaws worthy of condemnation or ridicule – and even certain barbaric traits – that call into question their claims to superiority. This article explores the mechanisms of this critique of ethnocentrism, which invites reflection on the relativity of customs. It also highlights the limits of this discourse – most notably Le Comte’s Christian-centric perspective, which sometimes leads him to deny Chinese alterity, for instance by portraying Confucius as a herald of the Messiah and China as a nation unconsciously shaped by Christianity.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Tree that Hides the Man: The Use and Misuse of Arboreal Symbols in Thomas of Woodstock (c. 1591-1595)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: “The huge greate Oke was once a plant.” This observation, found in Timothy Kendall’s anthology Flower of epigrammes (1577), seems to state the obvious: trees do grow from smaller (and frailer) plants and are subject to time. Yet this contrasts with the emblematic oak of early modern poetry and political theory – a symbol of strength, immutability, and royal majesty. As Andrew McRae (2012) notes, however, “the politics of the oak – and of trees more generally” – were not as settled in the sixteenth century as they would become later, thus paving the way for all sorts of rhetorical play. Focusing on the anonymous play Thomas of Woodstock (c. 1591-1595), this article explores how such arboreal symbols as the oak were manipulated and subverted on stage. This article argues that the play, in interrogating the use and misuse of trees – both as rhetorical tropes and as concrete natural elements – subtly challenges core tenets of royal orthodoxy. It questions the merging of the king’s two bodies and undermines the king’s uniqueness, thereby unveiling the fragility of symbols meant to uphold royal authority.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Fairy-Thinking and the Labyrinth: The Forest Palimpsest in Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1595)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream (1595), the forest outside Athens functions as an alternative space to the courtly world of supposed order and the rule of law. Constructed as a palimpsest of various layers, the forest is multi-faceted with shifting guises and roles. As a mirror to the court, it reflects government in a different form; and, as part of an ecology in crisis, it resonates with the flawed leadership and failed nurturing of patriarchal Athenian society. Maze-like and a place of wonder, the forest of A Midsummer Night’s Dream is both enchanting and threatening, as the motif of the labyrinth, with the Theseus and Minotaur intertext, haunts the forest. It is also a creative blank space, where desires and fears can be projected and encountered, offering a place to perform and rehearse the potential for tragedy and transformation. In the play, the fairies and the forest are closely aligned, both leading mortals astray and literalising the journey of the psyche through the labyrinth. This article argues that the interlinked fairies and forest are key to the play’s imaginary, and that their overlapping mythic intertexts enable thinking through human flaws and nurturing responsibilities. I conceptualise this as fairy-thinking, the projecting of the human into a magical green space. Through fairy-thinking, humans confront the other within themselves in negotiating the arboreal labyrinth and moving towards renewal.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Trees of the Muses in Aemilia Lanyer’s “The Description of Cooke-ham” (1611)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This essay analyses the symbolism of trees in Aemilia Lanyer’s poem “The Description of Cooke-ham” (1611) to highlight her mnemonic, protofeminist reconstruction of nature. Contrary to what other critics have suggested, the poem’s evocation of nature cannot be reduced to an early example of what John Ruskin called “pathetic fallacy”. While nature is presenting as feeling, it is not solely the projection of the persona’s emotions that are being expressed. The anthropomorphisation of trees acknowledges the alterity of nature as the speaker strives to offer an interpretation that does resonate with her own feelings as she leaves the estate. Their distinctive species and characteristics take on symbolic meanings that tie “The Description of Cooke-ham” to the long religious poem to which it was appended, Salve Deus Rex Judaeorum. Moreover, the references to Philomela and Echo – two myths that connect women’s experiences and nature – signal Lanyer’s poetic attempt to recover the valley of the Muses of Greek mythology by displacing it into an English pastoral context. More than landmarks that illustrate the poem’s topographical function, the trees of Cooke-ham are essential to Lanyer’s poetics by connecting the natural and the female in their commonality.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Of Trees, Harps and Lutes
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The intricate relationship between music, instruments, and trees in Elizabethan England is explored through an analysis of various literary and pedagogical texts of the period. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Reading the Early Modern Energy Crisis through Shakespeare: A Cultural History of Coal
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article draws attention to an overlooked phenomenon both in the history of early modern England and in the Shakespearean canon, namely coal and charcoal production at the turn of the seventeenth century. In early use, coal, which is duly mentioned in Shakespeare’s plays and poems, denoted mineral coal as well as charcoal but, in most cases, the playwright uses “coal” as synonymous with “charcoal”. This leads to two questions: why did the playwright seemingly promote charcoal over sea-coal at a time when the pollution resulting from domestic and industrial coal smoke was becoming perceptible? And what does this reality tell us about the early modern perspective on energy during a period of wood shortage? In order to address such questions, I would like to determine what can be more specifically learnt from the representation of charcoal – linked to wood felling and deforestation – in Shakespeare’s works: I pay attention not only to what he says about it, but also to what he does with it. I first turn to the plays in order to understand how they adumbrate a number of economic issues correlated to the use of charcoal, notably by dwelling on the figure of the collier with a series of puns exchanged by Sampson and Gregory in the opening scene of Romeo and Juliet, as well as on the early modern war industry, whose links with the theatre, which required canons, gunpowder and fireworks for its spectacular effects, are often underestimated. I then examine how Shakespeare refers to the production of charcoal in an era of severe environmental crisis. In this period marked by the depletion of English forests, the felling of wood for charcoal was particularly frowned upon, so that new strategies emerged, and coppicing, a technique mentioned in Love’s Labour’s Lost, became an alternative means of producing charcoal without infringing the law. Such economic and material considerations should not make us forget, however, the important role assigned to charcoal in aesthetic and cosmetic terms: the playwright must have been aware of its potentialities, and while he seems to reveal, in The Rape of Lucrece, a genuine familiarity with the techniques of painting, he also refers to the charcoal make-up of the actors playing Aaron, in Titus Andronicus, or Othello, in the tragedy of the same name. My chief objective here is to trace a number of silent connections between past and present and to engage in an ecocritical and aesthetic reflection on Shakespeare’s representation of the uses and misuses of energy.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: A survey of Mende adpositions
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: While a number of Mende grammars have been written (Aginsky 1935; Innes 1967; Spears 1967; Brown 1982), there is no systematic treatment of its adpositional system. In this paper I introduce Mende’s adpositional system, providing a brief, intuitive definition, according to Talmy’s (1983) schematization. I next consider how to categorize its adpositions as lexical, functional, or polyfunctional. I use five diagnostic tests to show how locatives are similar to putative nominals (and different from functional adpositions), then use two tests to show how they differ from nouns. Based on these tests, I propose a (synchronic) syntactic cline, ranging from nouns to light nouns to locatives and functional adpositions. Finally, I explore whether this analysis can also account for complex postpositions, arguing that the first adposition is always farther to the left on the cline.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Anarchism and Japan: for many, these two terms form a diametrically opposed couple. oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In Corsica, today, December 8 takes on a particular character, going beyond the simple religious framework (feast of the Immaculate Conception) to embrace a more identity and political aspect. Indeed, the island nationalist movement solemnly associates it with A Festa di a Nazione – The Nation’s Day -, which recalls that the island, in the 18th century, in rebellion against Genoa (from 1729), would have was placed under the protection of the Virgin on January 30, 1735, during a Cunsulta – Assembly – which took place in Corte. However, the date of January 30 is debated among some historians, as to its authenticity and the proclamation of December 8 as the Corsican Nation’s Day. This controversy is also fueled by the existence of another date, that of November 30, 1789, namely the accession of Corsica to the French Imperium – Empire – and to the principles of the Revolution. The significance of this event is further reinforced by the decision taken by the Assembly – Cunsulta – of Orezza, on September 23, 1790, to make November 30 the National Day of Corsica. Through these two dates, two conceptions of history appear in counterpoint: that of the national novel and that of historical authenticity.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Réflexions sur l’histoire populaire
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article reflects on the evolution, erosion, and contemporary necessity of people’s history as both a method and a political project. Emerging alongside modern historiography in the wake of the French Revolution, people’s history originally sought to centre the labouring classes, recover marginalised voices, and analyse society through the Marxist framework of class struggle. Foundational historians such as Michelet, Bloch, Thompson, Habib, and Rudé demonstrated that understanding social change requires attention to the lived experiences and contradictions shaping workers’ and peasants’ lives. From the late twentieth century onward, however, the rise of post-structuralism, cultural history, and post-Marxist thought shifted scholarship toward fragmented identities and away from class analysis, weakening the holistic, emancipatory ambitions of earlier “history from below.” The article also examines the growing divide between academic historiography and public engagement, driven by university privatisation, professionalisation, and the enclosure of knowledge behind paywalls. Against this backdrop, it argues for a renewed, politically committed history for the people—a practice rooted in mass education, collective intellectual life, and the battle of ideas. Drawing on the work of Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, it calls for rebuilding democratic historical consciousness as a foundation for contemporary struggles against capitalism, colonialism, and the far right.

L’existence d’appareils d’État puissants, la mise en œuvre de processus d’arraisonnement du territoire et d’articulation des souverainetés offraient une armature essentielle à l’inscription de la domination dans la durée, à la transformation de l’imperium en souveraineté royale, source de légitimité non seulement du pouvoir du roi, mais aussi des entités politiques qui lui étaient soumises. Pour comprendre ces phénomènes, il faut savoir dépasser la conception de l’État royal simplement spoliateur pour souligner, au contraire, ce qui était la condition d’une domination durable : les stratégies d’entretien, de protection et de préservation du territoire.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Par son brouillage des identités de genre, la France de Vichy est un lieu pertinent de l’histoire de la sexualité. L’affaire de Chalais, par la variété des points de vue qui la composent, permet de s’interroger sur les méthodes les plus adaptées à cette histoire. Le chevauchement de chronologie d’une part, l’enchevêtrement des événements d’autre part justifie le choix de recourir ici à une rétrospection micro-analytique. D’une « banale » affaire de collaboration charnelle, telle que les tribunaux de la Libération en voient alors défiler par centaines, les « événements » de Chalais viennent se situer à la croisée du politique et du sexuel. En 1942, l’application d’une directive sanitaire concertée entre le pouvoir vichyste et les autorités allemandes est le prétexte d’un charivari dans les rues de la petite ville de Chalais : des femmes suspectées de se prostituer, risquant par-là de contaminer des soldats allemands, sont attendues par une foule nombreuse sur le lieu de leur examen médical. Après coup, les exaspérations allemandes, l’opiniâtreté de gendarmes français et la ténacité de la réglementation des sexualités et du contrôle des corps sévissent dans la France de la Révolution nationale, de l’Occupation et de la Libération.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Archives du corps, archive de la biopolitique
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Le concept de biopolitique proposé par Foucault a non seulement suscité certains malentendus chez les historiens, mais il n’a en outre jamais été confronté à la question des archives susceptibles de lui donner corps. L’article s’appuie donc sur trois archives mineures, en marge des grands corpus de quadrillage et de surveillance classiquement étudiés. La première de ces archives est une liste de pratiques auto-érotiques d’un jeune allemand inverti, au début du xxe siècle. La confession écrite participe d’une économie générale des savoirs homosexuels qui se met en place autour d’une double instance du pouvoir, à la fois prise de contrôle médicale et potentiel foyer de résistance. La deuxième archive du biopolitique est un fragment de peau tatouée. Relevée sur le corps d’un soldat ou d’un bagnard, elle engage une recherche plus vaste encore des signes distinctifs, des marques reconnaissables. Ici la politique d’identification s’affronte aux pratiques de soi dans une ambiguïté renouvelée. Enfin, la troisième archive biopolitique présentée est une lettre de dénonciation des pratiques de prostitution dans une rue parisienne. L’anonymisation progressive de ces missives délatrices banalise un mode de surveillance policier qui intègre le dispositif de cartographie des mœurs en place dès la fin du xixe siècle.

In contrast, I analyse anarchist exile in the context of Italian migration, through the life of a key figure. In this light, anarchist exile no longer seems an aimless wandering, but rather a seamless and dense web of movements within a transnational community that comprised the Mediterranean Sea and the Atlantic Ocean. On the one hand, the study of anarchist exile adds to our understanding of Italian migration. Anarchist exile represented only a fraction of that migration, but it was a culturally significant component, which added its own dynamics to those of migration at large. Scottish literati explained the observable differences among peoples according to a universal pattern of development, from ‘savagery’ to ‘civil society’. The comparative perspective enabled the ‘savage’ and the ‘civil’ to be examined as subjects of societies on the same historical path, though progressing along it at different rates and in different times. Although this historical method meant that the ‘savage’ could become ‘civil’ by means of progress, the very principle of comparison raised two other problems : first, the problem of the social and cultural distance between different societies; second, the question of the unequal progress. Why had Amerindians remained in the ‘savage’ stage of hunting ? Why were the societies of Northern Europe considered the only ones to have completed all the stages of historic progress ? In seeking to explain the crucial question of non-homogeneous progress of human societies, Scotland’s Enlightenment literati deployed an analysis that came to rely on the concept of ‘race’.

L’auteur rappelle enfin que l’élection fut particulièrement serrée. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Chronique d’un non-lieu: le marxisme en Grande-Bretagne
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: La faiblesse de la diffusion du marxisme en Grande-Bretagne avant la Grande Guerre est un trait constaté par les contemporains, vérifié par les historiens, qui participe de la spécificité du travaillisme. Un examen plus approfondi de la question permet en réalité de mesurer l’importance de chronologies différenciées qui, toutes ensemble, empêchent le marxisme de devenir le discours commun du socialisme anglais. Les idées de Marx peinent à s’implanter parce qu’elles sont assez peu adaptées aux réalités politiques et sociologiques du monde ouvrier anglais, qui dispose déjà d’autres cadres d’interprétation pour expliquer son expérience historique. De plus, les partis ouvriers anglais qui apparaissent dans les années 1880 sont éclatés et ne permettent pas à une doctrine marxiste de devenir centrale. Enfin, celle-ci ne peut pas s’appuyer sur une traduction autorisée, dans la mesure où les textes de Marx sont disputés entre des groupes concurrents qui cherchent à asseoir leur légitimité. Le non-lieu britannique peut donc servir, plus généralement, à une histoire de la diffusion du marxisme en Europe en mettant en valeur trois conditions nécessaires : le monde ouvrier doit partager une expérience commune de l’industrialisation et de ses extrêmes, sans disposer pour autant de schémas interprétatifs convenus. Dans cet interstice, le marxisme parvient à s’implanter s’il est porté par un groupe politique qui entreprend sa diffusion à large échelle. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le radicalisme au début du xixe siècle, ou le poids des héritages
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Le radicalisme britannique postérieur à 1815 est le produit d’un faisceau d’influences plongeant en profondeur dans la culture politique britannique du xviiie siècle. En dépit des transformations que le radicalisme connaît au cours des premières décennies du xixe siècle, en particulier dans sa composition sociale, le poids des héritages reste déterminant jusqu’au vote du Great Reform Act. Le programme radical des années 1830 se présente comme le reflet fidèle de la plate-forme démocrate élaborée dès 1780 par John Cartwright. Considéré sous l’angle des moyens d’action, le radicalisme des années 1815-1832 est aussi l’héritier des méthodes mises sur pied par les pionniers du mouvement. Le recours aux pétitions aux temps forts de la campagne pour la réforme parlementaire fait écho à la campagne de Christopher Wyvill menée presque un demi-siècle plus tôt ou encore à l’action des abolitionnistes entre 1787 et 1792. Bien présente et très active dès les débuts du mouvement radical vers 1760-1770, la sphère extraparlementaire reste une donnée fondamentale du mouvement. C’est ainsi que la stratégie préconisée par Henry Hunt, visant à instaurer une instance représentative concurrente du Parlement, s’inscrit dans la droite ligne des initiatives prises par les radicaux de l’époque de la Révolution française qui entendaient réunir une Convention des délégués des sociétés populaires. Examinée dans sa globalité, des années 1760 jusqu’aux années 1830, l’histoire du radicalisme britannique laisse une impression puissante de répétition, l’essentiel ayant déjà été dit et produit entre 1770 et les années 1790.

Au cours des années 1820, autour de la figure de Jeremy Bentham, le radicalisme philosophique joue un rôle majeur, aux côtés du whiggisme, dans la redéfinition des termes de la vie politique britannique. Anglophiles, les libéraux français n’ignorent rien de ces débats et prennent position : si Madame de Staël et Benjamin Constant finissent par condamner les postulats utilitaristes, La Fayette et Jean-Baptiste Say, par exemple, entretiennent des liens étroits avec Bentham et ses disciples. Dix ans plus tard, Tocqueville se fera l’écho de l’ambivalence des libéraux français vis-à-vis de l’utilitarisme. à la fin du siècle, Élie Halévy opposera strictement un libéralisme français des droits de l’homme à un libéralisme anglais de l’utilité, contribuant à occulter durablement le rôle joué par l’utilitarisme dans la vie politique française de la chute de Napoléon à la Révolution de Juillet.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: À la fin des années 1960 s’affirme en Italie un autre football, dit de loisir, se voulant récréatif et non plus orienté par les exigences de la compétition. Il se joue à cinq ou à huit, sans arbitre et sur de petits terrains et est plébiscité par les pratiquants. Les structures d’encadrement traditionnelles, qu’elles soient catholiques ou communistes, s’adaptent à cette nouvelle demande : une nouvelle pédagogie, fondée sur le dialogue et refusant l’autoritarisme, semble nécessaire ; la participation à des championnats, voire l’existence de ces derniers, est remise en cause ; le modèle du professionnalisme, perçu comme facteur d’aliénation, doit être combattu sans relâche. Ces positions novatrices sont partagées tant par des militants-entraîneurs communistes de l’Union italienne du sport populaire (UISP) que par certains laïcs de l’Action catholique mobilisés au sein du Centre sportif italien (CSI). Des collaborations et des rapprochements s’esquissent même. Toutefois, ce mouvement rencontre de fortes oppositions, notamment au sein de l’association catholique. Au final, les divisions politiques perdurent, tandis que les nouvelles approches du jeu élaborées dans le contexte des années 1970 restent minoritaires.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: 1928-1929, « classe contre classe » : les sportifs ouvriers peuvent-ils se mesurer aux sportifs bourgeois ?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Au cours des années 1928-1929, la tactique « classe contre classe » promue par l’Internationale communiste et ardemment soutenue par les dirigeants des Jeunesses communistes français est imposée sans ménagement à la direction de la FST (Fédération sportive du travail), étroitement soumise au contrôle des JC. En interne, en France, les majoritaires s’opposent durement aux minoritaires « opportunistes » ou « liquidateurs » qui souhaitent que le mouvement sportif s’autonomise de cette tutelle trop politique, tandis qu’à l’Internationale, au moment des premières « Spartakiades » et du premier congrès de l’Internationale sportive rouge à Moscou au cours de l’été 1928, s’affrontent ceux qui préconisent l’entrisme dans les clubs sportifs « bourgeois » ou l’admission aux compétitions des jeunes ouvriers membres de ces clubs, et ceux qui s’y opposent. L’inflexion majeure contre cette tactique « sectaire » imposée au « sport ouvrier » en France s’opère avec la mise en retrait puis la mise à l’écart des dirigeants du groupe dit de la Jeunesse, en 1930 et 1931.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Aujourd’hui la plupart des historiens français rejettent le concept d’africanisme, pour des raisons semblables au rejet par Edward Said de l'Orientalisme, ou par Valentin Mudimbe de l’invention de l’Afrique. Plusieurs générations d’historiens africains formés aux Écoles de Dakar, de Dar es Salaam, ou d’Ibadan, nous rappellent désormais que ce que nous, Occidentaux, pensons être évident est loin de l’être pour l’Autre, et inversement. Les études africaines ne sont plus unilatérales. Elles sont aussi afrocentrées (ce qui ne signifie pas afrocentriques). C’est ce que rappellent les analyses dites postcoloniales1.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le « milieu » homosexuel suisse durant la Seconde Guerre mondiale
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Cette contribution s’intéresse à l’existence de lieux de sociabilité helvétiques entre hommes qualifiés comme étant homosexuels ou encore homoérotes selon le point de vue militant. Dans un pays resté neutre au cours de la Seconde Guerre mondiale et replié sur lui-même par « Défense nationale », fédéral depuis 1848 en unifiant trois cultures linguistiques, la capitale économique, Zürich, ressort sans conteste comme étant celle de l’homosexualité. Aussi cet article expose-t-il les conditions pénales expliquant l’existence dans cette ville de l’unique association homosexuelle qui va perdurer au-delà du conflit mondial. Il analyse aussi son mode de fonctionnement et revendicatif excluant progressivement les femmes de son sein. Toutefois, le monde associatif ne représente que la surface des événements, et cette étude s’attache à montrer les fortes différences existant selon les régions : la Zürich de la guerre ne s’est pas substituée au Berlin d’avant 1933, et les contrées latines, bien que profondément influencées par le code Napoléon, n’apparaissent pas comme des enclaves de liberté. Tolérance sociale relative et discrétion volontaire des intéressés, tels sont les mécanismes de cette histoire.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’idiotie contre la folie.
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Dans l’Antiquité, la « folie » représente un outil récurrent de la réflexion des auteurs chrétiens sur l’homme et son rapport à Dieu. Dans la controverse qui oppose Augustin aux pélagiens apparaît une nouvelle forme d’anomalie de l’esprit : l’« idiotie ». Le désaccord entre les deux parties porte avant tout sur le problème de la liberté de l’homme, soumis à des conceptions divergentes du corps conditionnant l’exercice de cette liberté. Il engage dès lors une lutte des savoirs sur l’homme, son corps, son âme, leur origine et leurs souffrances. Dans cette perspective, l’« idiotie », envisagée comme cas limite, est investie par Augustin d’une force d’exemplarité, au prix du déploiement de conceptions à première vue difficilement compatibles avec le discours chrétien sur la « folie ». Dans un cas comme dans l’autre, quoique de manière différenciée, l’enjeu pratique est pourtant le même : l’exercice du contrôle des corps, territoires de l’esprit.

La fin des années 1990 voit l’affirmation par des acteurs subalternes de demandes de reconnaissance et de réparations relatives cette fois au passé colonial de la France. Lors des commémorations du 150e anniversaire de l’abolition de l’esclavage en 1998, ces acteurs contestent le discours officiel des pouvoirs publics en revendiquant un récit alternatif fondé sur la notion de crime contre l’humanité. Face aux élites politiques hexagonales engagées dans l’adoption de « lois mémorielles », la formule « devoir de mémoire » a constitué alors un instrument de négociation pour les élites ultramarines devenues ainsi auteurs, par la voix de la députée Christiane Taubira, du « roman postnational » dans sa version postcoloniale.

Son intérêt pour le croisement entre histoire ouvrière et histoire du genre s’est manifesté notamment dans sa thèse, dirigée par Yves Lequin et publiée dans une version largement remaniée en 1993, avec Mathilde Dubesset, Parcours de femmes : réalités et représentations, Saint-Étienne (1880-1950)1. Elle vient de publier, en 2016, l’ouvrage important, la somme, une histoire « de la France », assumant par son titre un point de vue de lecture : « Des luttes et des rêves ». Cette dimension de choix assumé, renforcée par le sous-titre « Une histoire populaire » nous a, comme beaucoup d’autres, interpellés et nous a incités à interroger Michelle Zancarini-Fournel sur son projet. oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’État à la lettre
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Dans le passage problématique du moment politique renaissant à l’ère baroque, des administrateurs d’un genre nouveau contribuèrent, par leur expertise et leur capacité d’innovation technique et politique, à saturer de leur présence et de leur savoir-faire les secrétariats de la monarchie française. Ils créèrent ainsi, à l’échelle de leurs parentèles, des réflexes et des pratiques communes dans l’effectuation des décisions souveraines, jetant les bases d’un habitus de serviteur du roi, d’une langue et d’une science d’État. Autonomes dans un système aux normes qu’ils contribuèrent à inventer, prébureaucrates consacrés au service et aux volontés du prince, ils lièrent leur ascension à la montée en puissance de l’administration royale. Le moment politique des années 1560-1610 est une crise, au sens plein du terme : on passe d’un compromis politique à un autre, d’une architecture politique centrée sur la personne du souverain, veillant au fragile équilibre entre les cours et les communautés, à une autre configuration, où l’exaltation de la majesté royale de la nouvelle dynastie Bourbon est la principale charge de secrétaires et de conseillers puissants, dans l’immédiat entourage du souverain.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’État et la science
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Il est possible de caractériser le régime régulatoire organisant les rapports entre l’État et les sciences requises à son service par la mobilisation du droit, la professionnalisation des acteurs impliqués, l’édification d’une bureaucratie dédiée ainsi qu’un réseau de valeurs sur lesquelles reposent toutes les actions entreprises. Pour définir historiquement ce régime régulatoire, cet article envisage, pour la France, trois grandes époques qui singularisent des configurations spécifiques du rapport savoir/pouvoir. Du XVIe au XVIIIe siècle, la construction de l’État absolutiste moderne se fonde sur une politique des frontières, des cadastres et des sous-sols qui recourt à la géographie, la cartographie et la géologie pour asseoir sa légitimité. À partir de la fin du XVIIIe siècle et jusqu’aux années 1870, la biopolitique vise à maîtriser et contrôler les populations, leur état sanitaire et leurs intentions politiques. Enfin, depuis la IIIe République, la recherche d’une sécurité complète sur les choses et les hommes justifie une politique de la norme fixée par des indications scientifiques et techniques.

Dès lors, la sanction draine vers l’abbaye toute l’aile contestataire chrétienne qui va de la gauche à l’extrême gauche. À l’automne 1970, Boquen a pris le leadership des « chrétiens en recherche ». Les deux années qui suivent confirment son succès. Mais, en 1973, le déclin s’amorce. Il est aggravé par le départ de Bernard Besret en octobre 1974. À l’automne 1976, cette expérience utopique dans les murs de Boquen s’achève avec l’expulsion de la Communion et de la communauté des résidents qui s’y était établie. Comment cette petite abbaye cistercienne est-elle devenue ce laboratoire utopique de la vie communautaire, puis ce haut lieu de la contestation religieuse ?

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La personnification de la France dans la littérature de la fin du Moyen-Âge
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: À la frontière de l’histoire et de la littérature, l’étude rhétorique de la personnification de la nation dans la poésie d’Eustache Deschamps et de Christine de Pizan montre combien la création poétique contribua, au tournant des xive et xve siècles, à l’élaboration du concept quasi juridique de la nation comme personne morale intemporelle et supérieure, entretenant avec le roi ou la communauté des relations de personne à personne. Signe d’une fécondité littéraire qui refléterait – voire inspirerait – celle du droit, l’œuvre de ces deux auteurs offre, dans une profusion rare et selon un remarquable principe d’enrichissement poétique, l’ensemble des procédés rhétoriques qui créent la personnification : des plus simples, qui limitent la personne France à une voix désincarnée, aux plus complexes, qui dressent le tableau d’une belle femme désolée, abandonnée, allant jusqu’à l’insérer dans une trame relationnelle qui achève de l’instituer comme personne réelle et indépendante.
